literal: Reward will you get, O heart, to the cruel one my fading shoulders' distress having told?
translation: O heart, will you gain any reward by telling that cruel man about the distress of my wasting shoulders?
modern: நெஞ்சே! அந்தக் கொடியவரிடம் சென்று, மெலிந்து வாடும் எனது தோள்களின் துன்பத்தைச் சொல்வதால் நீ ஏதேனும் பயனைப் பெறுவாயா?
explanation: The heroine addresses her own heart, questioning the usefulness of sending a message to her absent lover. She calls him cruel because he has stayed away, causing her intense suffering. The word 'pūcal' usually means an uproar or battle, but here it vividly describes the intense distress of her wasting shoulders. She asks if there is any 'pāṭu' (which can mean greatness, but here means reward or benefit) in telling him of her physical decline, doubting that it will prompt his return.
